facts.statement: Tianyulong confuciusi was discovered in Jianchang County, Western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The only species is T. confuciusi, whose remains were discovered in Jianchang County, Western Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The genus Tianyulong was first named and described in 2006 by Xiao-Ting Zheng and colleagues.
facts.quote: Tianyulong confuciusi was first named and described in 2006 by Xiao-Ting Zheng and colleagues for a single fossil consisting of most of the skull and skeleton

facts.statement: The genus name Tianyulong refers to the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature, and the species name confuciusi honors Confucius.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the name of STMN that houses the specimen, while the species name is in honour of Confucius, the founder of Confucianism.

facts.statement: Uranium-lead dating of volcanic rocks overlying the fossil horizon suggests Tianyulong lived at least 158.5 million years ago during the Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: A sample from volcanic rocks overlying the Tianyulong horizon was dated through Uranium-lead dating to an age of 158.5 million years old, placing Tianyulong as at least as old and from the Middle Jurassic rather than later.

facts.statement: Based on comparisons with Heterodontosaurus, Tianyulong is estimated to have reached around 70 cm in total length, with the tail accounting for approximately 44 cm.
facts.quote: based on Heterodontosaurus it is estimated that Tianyulong reached around 70 cm in length, of which around 44 cm would have consisted of the tail.

facts.statement: Tianyulong possessed a skull that was especially large relative to its small neck and body.
facts.quote: Its skull was especially large compared to the small neck and body.

facts.statement: Tianyulong had extremely long hindlimbs with a tibia longer than the femur, while its forelimbs were very short, measuring less than 30% of the hindlimb length.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs were extremely long, with the tibia much longer than the femur, whereas the forelimbs were very short, less than 30% the length of the hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Tianyulong is known for a row of long, filamentous integumentary structures covering its back, tail, and neck.
facts.quote: Tianyulong has a row of long, filamentous integumentary structures on the back, tail and neck of the specimen.

facts.statement: The filamentous structures on Tianyulong are hollow, parallel, and singular without any evidence of branching.
facts.quote: The hollow filaments are parallel to each other and are singular with no evidence of branching.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the filamentous structures on Tianyulong are homologous to the proto-feathers found in theropods.
facts.quote: However, the homology between the ornithischian filaments and the theropods' proto-feathers is not obvious.

facts.statement: A study in Biology Letters tested the hypothesis that proto-feathers are primitive to dinosaurs and found support for the hypothesis that scales are the primitive trait instead.
facts.quote: A study published in the journal Biology Letters rigorously tested the hypothesis that protofeathers are plesiomorphic to dinosaurs. The results supported the hypothesis that scales are plesiomorphic to dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids, the group to which Tianyulong belongs, were likely herbivorous or possibly omnivorous.
facts.quote: They were herbivorous or possibly omnivorous.

facts.statement: Tianyulong lived at the end of the Jurassic period, approximately 158.5 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a fianles del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 158,5 millones de años, durante el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tianyulong was a subadult measuring approximately 70 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El holotipo es de un individuo del subadulto que midió probablemente 70 centímetros de longitud basada en las proporciones del género relacionado sudafricano Heterodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Tianyulong had unusual proportions compared to other heterodontosaurids, featuring a large head, long legs and tail, but short neck and forelimbs.
facts.quote: Tianyulong tenía proporciones inusuales en comparación con otros heterodontosáuridos. La cabeza era grande y las patas y la cola largas, pero el cuello y las extremidades anteriores eran cortos.

facts.statement: Tianyulong possessed a row of long, filamentous integumentary structures along its back, tail, and neck.
facts.quote: Tianyulong tiene una fila de estructuras tegumentarias largas y filamentosas en la espalda, la cola y el cuello del espécimen.

facts.statement: The estimated length of the integumentary structures on the tail was about 60 millimeters, which is seven times the height of a caudal vertebra.
facts.quote: La longitud estimada de las estructuras integumentarias en la cola es cerca de 60 milímetros que es siete veces la altura de una vértebra caudal.

facts.statement: Research by Lu et al. in 2010 re-dated the formation to the Late Jurassic, at least 158.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Lu et al. en 2010, informaron que estos lechos eran en realidad parte de la Formación Tiaojishan, que data del período Jurásico tardío hace al menos 158,5 millones de años.

facts.statement: A second specimen, IVPP V17090, was described in 2012.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen, IVPP V17090, se describió en 2012.

facts.statement: Tianyulong is classified as a heterodontosaurid, a group of small ornithischian dinosaurs characterized by a slender body, long tail, and enlarged canine-like teeth.
facts.quote: Tianyulong se clasifica como un heterodontosáurido, un grupo de pequeños dinosaurios ornitisquios caracterizado por un cuerpo delgado, la cola larga y un par de caninos agrandados como los colmillos.

facts.statement: Heterodontosaurids like Tianyulong were herbivores or possibly omnivores.
facts.quote: Eran herbívoros o posiblemente omnívoros.

facts.statement: The hollow filaments were parallel to each other, singular, and showed no evidence of branching.
facts.quote: Los filamentos huecos son paralelos entre sí y son singulares sin evidencia de ramificación.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the filaments of ornithischians like Tianyulong are homologous to the proto-feathers of theropods.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la homología entre los filamentos de los ornitisquios y las protoplumas de los terópodos no es evidente.

facts.statement: If homology is supported, it implies that the common ancestor of saurischians and ornithischians was covered in feather-like structures, and that groups known for skin impressions, like sauropods, were secondarily featherless.
facts.quote: Si se respalda la homología, la consecuencia es que el ancestro común de los saurisquios y los ornitisquios estaba cubierto por estructuras parecidas a plumas, y que los grupos por los que se conocen impresiones en la piel, como los saurópodos, solo estaban secundariamente sin plumas.

facts.statement: If homology is not supported, it suggests that these filamentous dermal structures evolved independently in saurischians, ornithischians, and other archosaurs like pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Si no se respalda la homología, indicaría que estas estructuras dérmicas filamentosas evolucionaron de forma independiente en saurisquios y ornitisquios, así como en otros arcosaurios como los pterosaurios.

facts.statement: The parent group of Tianyulong is Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Heterodontosauridae

facts.statement: Tianyulong belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for Tianyulong is from the Bathonian to the Kimmeridgian, between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)
